newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch central bank raises secured loans rate.
newsitem.headline: Dutch central bank raises secured loans rate.

text.p: The Dutch central bank said on Monday it was raising its key secured loans rate to 2.50 percent from 2.00 percent, effective from Tuesday.
The rate had been pegged at 2.00 percent since April 1996 when it was cut by 25 basis points.

The move was accompanied by an increase in the bank's special advances money market rate to 2.90 percent from 2.70 percent. The bank had raised the special advances rate to 2.70 percent from 2.50 percent at the end of February.
The secured loans rate is broadly similar to Germany's discount rate while the special advances rate is broadly similar to Germany's repo rate.

Economists and money market dealers had widely expected a further increase in the special advances rate this week, after the previous hike failed to reverse recent weakness of the Dutch guilder against the German mark.

Some had said the secured loans rate would probably also be raised if there was another substantial increase in the special advances rate, which the central bank usually adjusts by just 10 basis points at a time.
